finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: NOAA Fisheries says narwhals have two teeth in the upper jaw and the left tooth normally grows out through the front of the jaw in males (L463); overview identifies it as a tooth growing into the tusk (L408,L455). This makes “elongated tooth” the unique anatomical answer. “Horn” is a visual comparison only, lower jaw contradicts the source location, and a nasal bone is not the tooth NOAA identifies.
